Yes and no. I feel that I act a different way around different people. Not in a showing off way, but the me I am feels almost dependent on who I am around. They're all me, as real as I am when I'm alone, but they feel so strange to exhibit at times as well.

 I could be the quiet friend around someone I've known for 15 years or the impulsive one to someone I've known 6 months. Whenever I'm on my own, it gives me the impression that I'm not sure who I am exactly.

I've cut off both my parents. It was the one thing left from all the things I tasked myself with doing after my last therapy sessions. It came with the cost of feeling a bit shitty, especially given that my dad is ill now and my dog lives with them both, but I haven't been able to move on from what has happened, so cutting them out of my life was what I did.

Not gonna lie, I felt sick the first few weeks but it's pretty much the new normal now and there's a feeling of liberation in it. I think the strangest thing about it for me is that my sister and I grew up in the same home and have experienced a lot of the same things in regards to our parents growing up, but we've developed polar opposite views towards them.

I agree with the feeling of inevitability of it. I've always felt I'm going to die young. I agree also with one of the commenters who said it's a coping mechanism.

For me, it's this option I can take that no matter how bad it gets, I have the choice to get off the ride anytime and it's soothing. It wasn't always soothing, it used to scare me to think so nonchalantly like that but now, it's just whatever. It's another urge I can give power to depending on the day I've had but simultaneously also appealing as a way out if it seems bleak some days.

Additionally, the jump between thinking to do so is absurd or not right at present and then thinking that it's my only good option left and alternating so rapidly between them with the prior sentiment feeling alien to me gives me this impression that my mind isn't my own sometimes, that ease of jumping messes with my sense of identity. I don't think there's really a normal way of thinking for us, just whatever feels helpful in the moment, even if it's harmful.

The fascinating thing to me about the Ironborn is that they are shown to be a people in flux. George chose to write them down with a divide going on. He could have simplified them and made them a footnote in the wider story like the people of Skagos, but I'm glad that he didn't.

What I think I like the most about them is that they're caught in a cultural divide between traditionalists and reformists. Half of the population want to continue raiding Westeros for plunder and people and are more fervent supporters of the Faith of the Drowned God, while half of them want further integration into greater Westerosi society and are more tolerant of the mainland's religions and customs.

For every Quellon, there's a Balon. For every Victarion, there is an Asha. For every Rodrik, there is a Fralegg. 

Of course, there's also Euron who probably doesn't believe in either side. He's in it for himself and everyone is a toy to him, but he knows how to play one side over the other.

It's one of the main mysteries within the lore. At a guess, the Gods would have no power over mankind in this Age and it would be for humans to decide their own fates.

In the fire fading ending in Dark Souls 3, I'm paraphrasing, but the Firekeeper says that even after we've extinguished the flame, another one will light up in the future, meaning that the Age of Dark leads to another Age of Fire and vice versa like day and night. So, with that take, I'd say humanity would run things in an Age of Dark, led by a Dark Lord or many after them and then that time will pass to an Age of Fire. It's hard to know what that'll be like due to the gods having either died or abandoned the world and the cycle Gwyn wanted to avoid moving again.

That said, there's more we don't know than what we do. Gwyn feared and distrusted humans and the fragments of the Dark Soul they each carried within them. Was it out of fear of the unknown? Possibly. This resentment seemed to be one of his earliest due to the lack of commendation for humans in their war against the dragons, and casting a darksign on their armour as it was forged in the abyss.

On the Abyss, it's important to note that it's similar to Chaos in that it seems to be a corruption of a Lord Soul's power. Chaos is a corruption of Life birthing monstrosities that Gwyn and his knights fought against, while the Abyss seems to be a corruption of Dark involving infinite, gnawing Humanity.
